alternatives.root_cause: A downstream of checkout (kafka/broker or payment path) became slow, so frontend requests timed out and fraud-detection's consumer backed up.
alternatives.why_not: checkout itself never alerted, and fraud-detection's only edge in this graph is flagd, so a checkout-side slowdown does not cleanly explain its error burst.

alternatives.root_cause: flagd became slow or unreachable, so every service that blocks on flag evaluation stalled.
alternatives.why_not: cart, ad, recommendation and product-reviews all depend on flagd too and none of them alerted, which argues for a specific flag value rather than flagd being degraded.

verdict.summary: A feature flag was flipped in flagd, turning on a failing code path that is evaluated by several services at once - fraud-detection errors outright and the checkout/frontend request path degrades, surfacing as errors and latency at frontend-proxy and the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: The blast radius is the giveaway: frontend-proxy, frontend, load-generator, fraud-detection and flagd. fraud-detection has exactly one dependency in this graph - flagd - so an error burst there with no datastore or peer of its own points at a flag evaluation rather than an upstream call. At the same time the user-facing edge (load-generator -> frontend-proxy -> frontend) lights up with both errors and latency, which is the classic shape of a flag that degrades a shared path being consumed by both the checkout path and fraud-detection. A flag flip explains why multiple unrelated services break simultaneously with no artifact or config file change, and why flagd itself is in the traversal set but never alerts - flagd is healthy, it is serving a bad value. Onset is simultaneous across the edge rather than ramping, which argues against resource exhaustion or a slow dependency building up.
